purpose: Evaluate whether a requirements-to-acceptance-criteria capability preserves evidence, uncertainty, boundaries, and testable behavior across the curated product and discovery sources.

hard_failures.description: States an unsupported fact, metric, approval, customer quote, market claim, or commitment as known.
Drops a supplied rule, constraint, decision branch, guardrail, dependency, or failure condition that changes implementation or acceptance.
Produces acceptance criteria that cannot be observed, reproduced, or evaluated against explicit inputs and outcomes.
Silently fills an unknown, assumption, open question, dependency, or unresolved decision instead of preserving its status and required owner or evidence.
Commits to implementation, pixel-level design, approval, production action, or external evidence beyond the supplied authority and request.
Marks a requirement ready, validated, safe, or approved while a stated evidence, metric, risk, consent, dependency, or decision gate is unmet.
Assigns independent QA to modify product code or uses self-check evidence as an independent verdict.

checks: Each material claim links to supplied evidence, an explicit assumption, or an open question.
Evidence strength and freshness are not overstated.
Problem, affected users, behavior, pain, and business impact are distinct.
Personas and JTBD are not presented as facts without support.
Functional behavior, states, constraints, dependencies, scope, risks, and open questions are retained.
Out-of-scope items include a reason when one is available.
Every acceptance criterion has observable preconditions, action or event, and expected result.
Error, boundary, recovery, and non-regression behavior is explicit when relevant.
Needs-input, blocked, assumption, and validated states are distinguished.
Readiness and risk gates do not silently pass.
The output stays at requirements and acceptance-contract level.
It does not claim design, implementation, approval, or external execution without authority.
Identifiers, assumptions, rules, evidence links, and unresolved items survive handoff to engineering, QA, or roadmap work.

review_protocol.automatic: Check hard failures, required fields, identifiers, source references, unknown markers, AC observability, and gate decisions.
review_protocol.blind_human: Review candidate and baseline outputs under anonymous labels; score dimensions and record rationale for every score below maximum.
review_protocol.holdout_policy: Do not modify candidate guidance or rubric from holdout outputs before candidate freeze.
